sections.heading: 1. Describing Motion
points: **Motion** = change of position with time, relative to a **reference point**.
**Distance** = total path length covered (a **scalar**, has only magnitude).
**Displacement** = the **shortest** distance from start to finish, with direction (a **vector**).
Displacement can be **zero** even when distance is not (e.g. returning to the start).

sections.heading: 2. Speed, Velocity and Acceleration
points: **Speed = distance ÷ time** (scalar); SI unit **m/s**.
**Velocity = displacement ÷ time** (vector — speed in a given direction).
**Acceleration** = rate of change of velocity (**a = (v − u)/t**); SI unit **m/s²**.
**Uniform motion** = equal distances in equal times (constant velocity, zero acceleration); **non-uniform** = changing velocity.

sections.heading: 3. Equations of Motion (uniform acceleration)
points: **v = u + at**
**s = ut + ½at²**
**v² = u² + 2as**
(u = initial velocity, v = final velocity, a = acceleration, s = displacement, t = time).

sections.heading: 4. Graphs and Circular Motion
points: **Distance–time graph:** slope = **speed**; straight line = uniform motion.
**Velocity–time graph:** slope = **acceleration**; area under it = **distance**.
**Uniform circular motion** — moving in a circle at constant speed, but velocity **changes** (direction changes) → it is **accelerated** motion.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Distance = scalar (path length); displacement = vector (shortest, with direction); displacement can be 0.
Speed = distance/time; velocity = displacement/time; acceleration = (v−u)/t (m/s²).
Equations: v = u+at; s = ut+½at²; v² = u²+2as.
Distance–time slope = speed; velocity–time slope = acceleration, area = distance.
Uniform circular motion = constant speed but changing velocity → accelerated.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Distance is a scalar**; **displacement is a vector** and can be **zero** even when distance is not.
**Speed** uses distance; **velocity** uses displacement (with direction).
On a **velocity–time graph**, the **slope = acceleration** and the **area = distance**.
**Uniform circular motion is accelerated** because the direction (velocity) keeps changing.
